preamble: The glottal stop [ʔ] is replaced by the palatal glide [j], typically next to front vowels or in hiatus where the glide is the natural transition. Assyrian Neo-Aramaic and Turoyo turned inherited word-initial /ʔ/ into /j/ in most dialects (Aramaic arrīḵā > yarīḵā 'long'); Levantine and Hijazi Arabic replace Classical Arabic hamza after long ā with y in active participles (nāʔim > nāyim 'sleeping'); and Persian adapted the same Arabic medial hamza as y in loanwords (jāʔiza > jāyiza 'prize').
